body_markdown:
```text

In the middle of October, Reddit started refusing NewsBlur’s requests for subreddit feeds, and by early November every Reddit feed in NewsBlur had stopped updating. It came up on the forum right away. Reddit is also retiring its RSS feeds.

``` Since November 10, NewsBlur gets Reddit posts from[RedListen](https://redlisten.com/) , a service that serves Reddit’s own listings. Subreddit, user, multireddit, comment, and search feeds all update again, and you don’t need to change anything. ### What’s different RedListen has a monthly limit on how many posts it returns, so NewsBlur reads Reddit a little differently than it used to: - **Subreddits are checked about once an hour,** many at a time. Quiet subreddits get every post. The busiest ones get a share of their posts, and that share grows with the number of NewsBlur readers following them. - **Hot and Top feeds read the same as New.** - **Reddit’s front page, r/all, and r/popular aren’t available,** and those feeds will say so. - **Comment thread and search feeds update at most twice a day,** and less often while they’re quiet. Comment threads older than 30 days can’t be fetched anymore. - **Refreshing a Reddit feed yourself still fetches it right away,** and so does adding a new one. - **Posts keep their formatting.** Reddit sends post text as plain text with formatting marks, and NewsBlur turns it into paragraphs, links, emphasis, code, quotes, and lists. Images come through too. - **Personal Reddit RSS feeds,** the ones with` ?feed=` in the address, still come straight from Reddit for as long as Reddit serves them. ### Availability It’s been live since November 10. It all happens on NewsBlur’s servers, so it works on the web and in every app without an update. If a subreddit isn’t coming through the way you’d expect, let me know on the[NewsBlur forum](https://forum.newsblur.com/) . --- This is a companion discussion topic for the original entry at[https://blog.newsblur.com/2026/11/21/reddit-feeds-are-back/](https://blog.newsblur.com/2026/11/21/reddit-feeds-are-back/)
